features.baseline_contract: Universal Intel and Apple Silicon executable; minimum macOS 14.0. SwiftUI, AppKit, WebKit, native document windows.
Remarque; “Markdown. Beautifully refined.” Bundle ID `ca.forensicintelligence.remarkable` retains the former Remarkable name.
Documents remain user-owned UTF-8 text, not an application database format.
`.md`, `.markdown`, `.mdown`, standard Markdown UTI, legacy application Markdown UTI, and plain text.
Native New command and start-window New Document / Blank Document.
Native file picker and recent-document opening; tested opening the local feature probe.
Start-window list and native Open Recent list; names, location context, Clear Menu.
Save, Save As, Duplicate, Rename, Move To, Revert To, Share; native command enablement depends on the active document.
Separate document windows; native tab bar and tab overview appear with document windows.
Close, Close All, minimize/zoom, full screen, Bring All to Front, macOS tiling/arrangement.
Status bar reports Saved or document modification state; edits must participate in the document lifecycle.
Clean document reloads automatically; unsaved edits prompt to reload/discard or keep editing.
Error paths for unsupported type, invalid UTF-8, unreadable/empty file, encoding failure, open/save failure.
Release notes promise atomic export writes so failed output does not destroy a previous file.
About, Settings, Services, Hide, Hide Others, Show All, Quit, Quit and Keep Windows.
Local document processing, no account/cloud/telemetry dependency. Bundled rendering assets verified; absence of network traffic is not proven.
Sandboxed file access, remembered security-scoped folder bookmarks for sibling images and custom stylesheets.
One-time folder-access prompt and a Grant Access banner after decline; grants also support export.
Brand/sidebar; New Document, Open, Documentation, recent files, Open Other. Show Start Window command.
Empty Markdown document.
Welcome, outline guidance, formatting shortcuts, flowchart with layout metadata, export comparison table. Opened during audit.
Overview, goals, architecture diagram, risks/tasks, references.
Meeting title, date, attendees, agenda, notes, action-item tasks.
Named flowchart with size/alignment metadata and decision branches.
Problem, solution, and milestone table.
Welcome, structured writing, diagramming, export, privacy, and setup-default pages. Image storage and default export choices.
Versioned release highlights; remembered last-seen version/onboarding state.
Dedicated window, searchable sidebar, 19 help articles. Full article evidence retained.
Syntax examples for headings, marks, lists, links, images, tables/alignment, callouts, math, details, front matter.
Diagram examples/templates, source insertion, and visual-editor entry for supported types.
Dedicated window plus Settings Keyboard and documentation article.
Version/product attribution and Forensic Intelligence website. External link not followed during audit.
Source editor alone.
Side-by-side source and typeset preview.
Source and structural navigation.
Outline, source editor, preview; observed on launch of test documents.
Preview-only proofreading.
Generated source, interactive canvas, inspector; distinct document layout.
Adjustable pane widths; stored outline/preview width and last-layout fields exist.
Toolbar/menu commands toggle preview and outline.
Hierarchical headings, current-section highlighting, heading count, click-to-source navigation.
Optional diagram entries labelled by metadata title or diagram source/type.
Unique IDs generated, e.g. `repeated-heading` and `repeated-heading-1`; verified in HTML output.
Hides chrome, readable centered column, optional inactive-paragraph dimming.
Keeps caret line vertically centered.
Setting advertises source-to-preview and preview-to-source scrolling. Precise behavior differs by engine and needs regression testing.
Word count, reading minutes, diagram count, source line/column, layout name, saved state.
In-app slide overlay, slide counter, exit control, documented arrows/Space/Escape. Probe reported 12 slides; see discrepancy record.
No headings, nothing to present, no recents, no workspace folder, no versions, no matching commands.
Ordinary HTML preview heading click did not move source cursor. This is a requested new feature, not established baseline behavior.
AppKit text engine; selection, caret, copy/cut/paste/delete/select-all, keyboard movement and native undo/redo.
Markdown structure, subdued markers, headings, links, Mermaid fence tint; incremental styling documented.
Optional preview/export highlighting; Swift, JS/TS, Python, Go, Rust and other languages documented.
Enabled in observed settings; disables smart behaviors for plain source editing.
Toggle whole styled span under caret, or current word without selection; avoid repeated marker stacking, including nested emphasis.
Tab at line start cycles body/H1/H2/H3/body.
Return continues bullets, numbering or task boxes; automatic numbering; empty item Return exits list.
Smart quote continuation is explicitly advertised in Editing settings.
Tab/Shift-Tab on list lines; snippet expansion shares Tab.
Brackets, parentheses and quotes pair or wrap selected text.
HTML/Word rich text becomes Markdown headings, marks, links, code, and lists; switchable.
Clipboard/Finder images become Markdown references and stored media.
Dropping a URL on selected text makes a Markdown link.
Spellcheck, smart quotes, smart dashes, soft wrap preferences; OS dictation and Emoji & Symbols menus.
Conceals source markers and provides in-place math/Mermaid tiles; entering a block reveals source. Toggle and same source-editing surface observed; full tile behavior needs further testing.
Existing ribbon is above the **left/source pane**. Style selector, bold, italic, strike, highlight, inline code, table alignment, text-size control.
Body, Heading 1–6, Quote; applies to current source line.
Left/center/right commands enabled in table context.
Left/center/right table placement stored using an HTML comment.
Ribbon text-size stepper scales source and preview together; observed source size 15 pt.
Bold, italic, strike, inline code, heading, blockquote, bullet/number/task lists, link, image, table editor, code fence, equation, rule, Mermaid. Hide/show command.
Bold, italic, inline code, code block, link, image, equation, heading, blockquote, lists, table editor, quick table, horizontal rule.
Helpers wrap selection or insert a placeholder; source edits participate in undo.
One undoable pass normalizing whitespace/list markers/table columns. Preserve code/math content, rules, hashtags and hard breaks.
Native AutoFill, dictation, Emoji & Symbols, document/tab/window controls; some depend on macOS/context.
H1–H6; heading hierarchy and IDs. H1/H2 exercised; other levels exposed by styles.
Underlined headings; `===` form exercised.
Paragraph separation, soft wrapping, trailing-space hard line breaks.
Strong/emphasis/nested combination with asterisk and documented underscore forms.
Literal code spans; underscores preserved in rendered `inline_code`.
Language annotation, code rendering/highlighting, four-backtick outer fence exercised.
`==text==`; HTML uses contrasting mark colors, including inline code inside marks.
Named shortcodes, aliases such as `:+1:`, broad embedded name table; `:rocket:` exercised.
Nested unordered lists.
Explicit start number and mixed/nested ordered/unordered children.
Checked/unchecked task syntax. HTML preview checkboxes are disabled in the baseline.

Rule rendering; formatter promises preservation.

Definitions reused in paragraphs and table cells.
Inline/block Markdown images, reference images, local assets, data URIs, alt text.

Header/divider/body, inline formatting and links in cells, column alignment and escaped pipes.

NOTE, TIP, IMPORTANT, WARNING, CAUTION; titles and body formatting.

Definitions/references; numbered section at document end and links to it.

Optional readable HTML comment storing diagram identity, title, size, alignment and source-display choices. Legacy `remarkable:mermaid` recognized in binary.
Escaped table pipe, literal snake_case, longer code fences verified; broad conformance suite still required.

HTML engine selected initially; styled headings/text/tables, rendered math and diagrams. Related setting says matching print.
SwiftUI-native rendering and interactive diagram cards; manually switched to inspect, then restored.

Default-browser preference; wiki/local-note routing; internal heading and footnote links.
